mainTopic: End of the dispute about a טומטום who was found to be a סריס (practical differences for חליצה), the הדרן closing פרק על אלו מומין, and the opening of the new פרק: animal blemishes also disqualify a כהן, plus head-shape blemishes unique to people.
overview: First, the גמרא finishes an earlier discussion about a טומטום who was found to be male. It gives two practical differences between רבי יהודה (he is definitely a סריס חמה) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (he is only possibly a סריס), both about חליצה. Then the הדרן closes the chapter על אלו מומין. A new משנה teaches that every blemish that disqualifies an animal also disqualifies a כהן. It adds blemishes found only in people: odd head shapes, a hunched back (debated by רבי יהודה and the חכמים), and baldness. The גמרא asks how the lists can match when some blemishes are written only for people and others only for animals. It answers with a גזירה שוה from the words גרב and ילפת, which are extra in the verses. It then explains why the Torah still writes two lists: each kind has blemishes the other cannot have, and the Torah repeats a passage for the sake of something new. רבא shows that the basic rule of מום had to be written separately for a כהן, קדשים and a בכור. Finally, רבי יוחנן derives the extra human blemishes from מזרע אהרן: a כהן must look like the other כהנים.

steps.title: Two practical differences between the two opinions about the טומטום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers what the practical difference is between רבי יהודה (definitely a סריס חמה) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (only possibly a סריס). The differences are disqualifying the widow when other brothers exist, and requiring חליצה when no other brothers exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is in two cases: disqualifying the widow from the other brothers when there are other brothers, and the need to do חליצה when there are no other brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier question: since both opinions agree this טומטום should not do חליצה, what practical difference is there between them? It gives two cases where they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, he is definitely a סריס חמה, so his חליצה means nothing. When other brothers exist, she may still do יבום with one of them. When no other brothers exist, she needs no חליצה at all. For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, he might be a normal male, so his חליצה might count. That would forbid her to the other brothers, and when he is the only brother, she must get חליצה from him to be safe.

keyTerms.meaning: to disqualify. Here it means making the widow forbidden to the other brothers through his חליצה.
where there are other brothers of the dead husband
to perform חליצה, the ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
there is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Both cases involve the same person, a טומטום found to be male. The difference is only whether there are OTHER brothers. With brothers, the question is whether his חליצה ruins her chance of יבום with them. Without brothers, the question is whether she needs חליצה from him at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic גמרא tool. When two opinions seem to give the same ruling, the גמרא looks for a case where 'definitely' and 'maybe' lead to different results.

phrases.english: To disqualify where there are brothers,
phrases.notes: Does his חליצה forbid her to the other brothers? According to רבי יהודה it does not. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה it does, out of doubt.

phrases.english: and to perform חליצה where there are no brothers,
phrases.notes: According to רבי יהודה no חליצה is needed. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה she needs חליצה, out of doubt.

phrases.english: there is a difference between them.
phrases.notes: Answers the question 'מאי בינייהו' on the previous amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier about the practical difference between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical difference is there between calling him a definite סריס חמה and a possible סריס?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two cases: (1) whether his חליצה disqualifies the widow from the other brothers; (2) whether she needs חליצה from him when he is the only brother.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Definitely a סריס חמה' (רבי יהודה) means his חליצה is meaningless. 'Maybe a סריס' (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה) means we must be strict both ways.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter על אלו מומין
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing formula marks the end of the chapter על אלו מומין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter על אלו מומין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter על אלו מומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses love for the learning and a commitment to come back and review it. That chapter listed the blemishes that let a בכור animal be slaughtered outside the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you. This is the formula said when finishing a chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Al Elu Mumin.'
phrases.notes: Chapter name taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter על אלו מומין is complete.

steps.title: Animal blemishes also disqualify a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that every מום taught for animals, whether permanent or temporary, also disqualifies a כהן from serving in the מקדש. It then announces that people have additional blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: These blemishes, whether permanent or temporary, disqualify a person. And there are more blemishes in addition to them:
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with its basic rule: the animal blemishes from the earlier chapters apply to a כהן too. The last phrase ('in addition to them') sets up a list of extra human blemishes that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the laws of בעלי מומים for animals to the laws for כהנים. Even a temporary blemish disqualifies a כהן while he has it. The words וְיָתֵר עֲלֵיהֶן tell us the human list is longer than the animal list.

keyTerms.meaning: short for מַתְנִיתִין, meaning 'our משנה'
blemishes or physical defects
permanent
temporary, passing
disqualify a person, meaning a כהן from doing the עבודה
and there are more in addition to them

steps.confusionAlert: 'Disqualify a person' does not mean the person is no longer a כהן. He keeps his status as a כהן and only cannot perform the עבודה while he has the blemish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the foundational rule for the whole chapter: one shared list of מומים governs both קרבנות and the כהנים who offer them.

phrases.english: MISHNA: These blemishes,
phrases.notes: Refers to the blemishes listed for animals in the earlier chapters.

phrases.english: whether permanent or temporary —
disqualify in a person,
phrases.notes: Meaning a כהן is barred from the עבודה.

phrases.english: and in addition to them:
phrases.notes: Sets up the list of blemishes that apply only to people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All animal blemishes, permanent or temporary, disqualify a כהן from the עבודה, and people have additional blemishes beyond these.

steps.title: Extra blemishes for people: abnormal head shapes
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing blemishes found only in people, all about the shape of the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pointed head, a turnip-shaped head, a hammer-shaped head, a head with a dent, and a head that sticks out in the back.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now delivers the list promised in the last step. It names five unusual head shapes that disqualify a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are blemishes animals are not listed with, so the משנה names them separately. The כילון is narrow on top and wide below, and the לפתן is wide on top and narrow below. The מקבן has a forehead that juts out like a hammer, the שקוט has a dent in the head, and the סקיפת has a back of the head that sticks out.

keyTerms.meaning: head pointed on top, narrow above and wide below
turnip-shaped head, wide above and narrow below
hammer-shaped head with a protruding forehead
his head has a dent or sunken spot
the back of the head sticks out

phrases.english: the pointed-headed one, and the turnip-headed one,
and the hammer-headed one, and one whose head is indented,
and one whose back of the head protrudes.
phrases.notes: The משנה's list continues next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the 'additional blemishes' announced by וְיָתֵר עֲלֵיהֶן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Abnormal head shapes (כילון, לפתן, מקבן, שקוט, סקיפת) are blemishes that disqualify a כהן.

steps.title: Dispute about a hunchbacked כהן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of human blemishes. רבי יהודה rules that a hunchbacked כהן is fit, and the חכמים rule that he is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And hunchbacks: רבי יהודה says they are fit, and the חכמים say they are disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps listing blemishes found only in people. Here it records a disagreement about a hunched back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בעלי חטרות are people with a humped back. רבי יהודה does not consider this a disqualifying blemish, so the כהן may serve. The חכמים say it is a blemish, so he may not serve.

keyTerms.meaning: Hunchbacks, people with a humped back
Rules that he is fit (allowed to serve)
Rule that he is disqualified

phrases.english: And those with humped backs —
phrases.notes: A new item in the list of human blemishes. It is about the back, not the head.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda deems them fit,
and the Sages disqualify them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַעֲלֵי חֲטָרוֹת רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of human blemishes from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hunchback: רבי יהודה says the כהן is fit; the חכמים say he is disqualified.

steps.title: A bald כהן is disqualified, and the definition of bald
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a קרח is disqualified. It defines a קרח as someone who has no strip of hair running around the back of the head from ear to ear. If he has that strip, he is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bald man is disqualified. Who counts as bald? Anyone who does not have a line of hair going around from ear to ear. If he has one, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more head blemish, baldness, and then defines exactly how bald someone must be to be disqualified.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being bald on top of the head is not enough to disqualify. What matters is the band of hair that goes around the back of the head from one ear to the other. If that band is missing, he is a קרח and may not serve. If it is there, he is fit even though the top of his head is bald.

keyTerms.meaning: A bald person
A line or strip of hair
Going around from ear to ear
Fit to serve

steps.whatToRemember: A קרח is defined by the band of hair from ear to ear, not by baldness on top. If the band is there, the כהן is fit.

phrases.english: The bald man is disqualified.
Who is considered bald?

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שִׁיטָה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר
phrases.english: Anyone who does not have a line of hair
that goes around from ear to ear;
phrases.notes: This means around the back of the head.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ — הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר.
phrases.english: if he has one, he is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another head blemish to the list and defines it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרח is disqualified; a קרח is someone with no band of hair from ear to ear.

steps.title: Some blemishes are written only for animals and others only for people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that every animal blemish also disqualifies a כהן. A יבלת is written in the Torah only for animals. דק and תבלול are written only for people, yet they were counted as animal blemishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? But there is a wart, which is not written in the Torah for a person! And also: a cataract and a תבלול, which are not written for an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now begins and attacks the משנה's opening rule (step 3) that people and animals share the same blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's list of animal blemishes includes יבלת, but the list for a כהן does not. The list for a כהן includes דק and תבלול, but the animal list does not. So how can the משנה say the blemishes are the same, and how were דק and תבלול counted as animal blemishes earlier?

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
A wart
A cataract / film over the eye
An eye blemish where the white enters the dark part
And furthermore

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge works in both directions. יבלת is missing from the list for people, and דק and תבלול are missing from the list for animals.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why? But there is a wart,
phrases.notes: The question targets the משנה's rule that every animal blemish disqualifies a כהן.

phrases.english: which is not written in the Torah regarding a person!
And furthermore: a cataract and a tevallul,
which are not written regarding an animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins by challenging the משנה's general rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that all animal blemishes also disqualify a כהן (and the earlier listing of דק and תבלול as animal blemishes).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's verses list different blemishes for people and for animals, so the two lists do not seem to match.

steps.title: The two lists are learned from each other by a גזירה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the blemishes of people and animals are learned from each other. It quotes a ברייתא: the shared words גרב and ילפת, which appear in both lists, form a גזירה שוה that moves each list's blemishes to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn from each other, as a ברייתא teaches: for a person, a wart is not stated; for an animal, a cataract and תבלול are not stated. From where do we know to apply what is said of one to the other, and what is said of the other to the first? The verse says 'scab' and 'scab,' 'scurvy' and 'scurvy,' for a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even though each blemish is written in only one place, a גזירה שוה makes the two lists into one shared list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words גרב and ילפת appear both in the verse about a blemished כהן and in the verse about a blemished animal. That shared wording links the two passages. So יבלת is applied to people, and דק and תבלול are applied to animals.

keyTerms.meaning: From each other
As a ברייתא teaches
A type of scab or dry skin rash
A type of skin disease (scurvy)
A teaching drawn from the same word appearing in two places

steps.whatToRemember: Blemishes of a כהן and of an animal are one shared list, linked by the גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת.

phrases.english: They are derived from one another,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Regarding a person, a wart is not stated,
regarding an animal, a cataract and tevallul are not stated.

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן אֶת הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what is said of this one to that one,
and what is said of that one to this one?
The verse states: 'scabbed' and 'scabbed,'
phrases.notes: The word appears both in Leviticus 21:20 (a כהן) and in Leviticus 22:22 (an animal).

phrases.english: 'scurvy' and 'scurvy,' for a verbal analogy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source derivation: a גזירה שוה joins the two lists.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each blemish applies only where the Torah wrote it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of the גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת, every blemish applies to both people and animals.

steps.title: The words must be extra, or the comparison could be broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the words used for this גזירה שוה must be 'free' (extra in the verse). Otherwise, the comparison could be refuted: an animal is stricter because it goes on the מזבח, and a person is stricter because he is commanded in מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They must be free. For if they are not free, it could be refuted: a person cannot be learned from an animal, since the animal itself is offered on the altar; an animal cannot be learned from a person, since a person is included in the commandments.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its answer. It explains that this גזירה שוה only works if the words are extra, and it sets up the next move, which is proving that they really are extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה built on words that are not extra can be broken by showing a real difference between the two cases. Here each side has its own reason to be stricter: an animal is itself brought on the מזבח, and a person carries the obligation of מצוות. So the words גרב and ילפת must be extra in the verses for the link to hold.

keyTerms.meaning: Free / extra in the verse, available for the גזירה שוה
To refute (by showing a difference)
Is offered on the altar
Is included in (obligated in) מצוות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two arguments. The animal is stricter because of the מזבח, and the person is stricter because of מצוות. Each argument blocks learning in one direction.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule: a גזירה שוה whose words are not extra can be broken by a logical difference between the cases. That is why the גמרא next needs to prove the words are extra.

phrases.english: They must be free (superfluous),
phrases.notes: The words must be extra in the verse so the גזירה שוה cannot be refuted.

phrases.english: for if they are not free, it can be refuted:
a person cannot be derived from an animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הִיא עַצְמָהּ קְרֵיבָה לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ;
phrases.english: since the animal itself is offered on the altar;
an animal cannot be derived from a person,
since a person is included in the commandments.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְנֵי דְּאִי לָא מַפְנֵי אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the גזירה שוה of step 8 by requiring that the words be extra, and anticipates a possible refutation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת holds only if the words are extra, because otherwise the differences between people and animals would refute it.

steps.title: Proving the words are truly 'free'
steps.stepSummary: The word גרב is extra, because it could be learned from ילפת with a קל וחומר. So it is free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the objection does not apply, because the words are free. The Torah could have written only 'ילפת' and left out 'גרב.' I would have reasoned: if ילפת, which is not repulsive, is a blemish, then surely גרב, which is repulsive, is a blemish. So why did the Torah write 'גרב'? To make it free for the גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry from the last step. It shows that the words of the גזירה שוה really are extra, so nobody can refute it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ילפת, a less disgusting skin condition, counts as a blemish, then גרב, which is more disgusting, obviously counts too. The Torah did not need to write גרב, so the word is extra. An extra word is 'free' for a גזירה שוה, and the refutations ('an animal goes on the מזבח,' 'a person is commanded in מצוות') no longer matter.

keyTerms.meaning: They are truly free (extra words in the verse)
Repulsive, disgusting
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah or ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the קל וחומר is the source for the blemishes. It only shows that the word גרב is not needed for its plain meaning, so it is free for the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: No, they are indeed free (extra),
phrases.notes: Rejects the possibility that the words are not free.

phrases.english: let the Merciful One write 'scurvy'
and there would be no need for 'scab',
and I would say:
if scurvy, which is not repulsive,
is a blemish,
then a scab, which is repulsive, all the more so!
The word 'scab' that the Merciful One wrote,
why do I need it? To make it free (for the גזירה שוה).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes Step 9 by showing the גזירה שוה words really are free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof that a word is superfluous (קל וחומר makes it extra)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the words גרב and ילפת are needed for their plain meaning, so the גזירה שוה could be refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: גרב can be learned from ילפת by a קל וחומר, so it is extra and the גזירה שוה stands.

steps.title: Why not list all blemishes in one place?
steps.stepSummary: If the lists are learned from each other anyway, the Torah should have written every blemish in one list, and written only גרב and ילפת in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Torah write all the blemishes in one place, write גרב and ילפת here and there, and let the rest be learned from that one list!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the Torah's repetition. Since the גזירה שוה carries everything across, why write the full list twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the two lists are learned from each other. If so, writing them both in full seems wasteful. Writing one full list plus the two shared words would be enough to transfer everything.

keyTerms.meaning: In one (place or list)
Here and here, in both places
And let them be learned from one

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write all of them in one (place),
and scab and scurvy here and here,
and let them be learned from the one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the גזירה שוה is secure, the גמרא asks why the Torah repeats the lists.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Torah's choice to list blemishes separately for people and for animals.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a גזירה שוה transfers every blemish, one full list plus the two shared words would be enough, so the second list seems extra.

steps.title: If written only for people, animal-only blemishes would be lost
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah listed everything for אדם, we would think only human blemishes apply to animals. Then קלוט and חוטין would not disqualify an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: In which of them should the Torah write it? If it wrote it for a person, I would say: whatever disqualifies a person disqualifies an animal. Then קלוט and חוטין, which do not exist in people, would not disqualify an animal either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by testing the first option: putting the full list only in the section about כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה moves the list from one side to the other, but it only moves what is written. Blemishes that cannot happen to people, like closed hooves (קלוט) or damaged gums (חוטין), would never be written in a human list. So they would never reach animals.

keyTerms.meaning: On which, in which (of the two)?
An animal with closed, uncloven hooves
Damaged gums (an animal-only blemish)
I would have thought

phrases.english: On which, in which one should the Merciful One write it?
If He wrote it regarding a person, I would say:
whatever disqualifies in a person disqualifies in an animal,
but closed hooves and damaged gums, which do not exist in a person,
would not disqualify in an animal either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11 by testing the first option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that each list holds unique items that the other list cannot carry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One full list would be enough, since the גזירה שוה transfers it.
steps.terutzMaskana: A human-only list would leave out animal-specific blemishes like קלוט and חוטין.

steps.title: If written only for animals, human-only blemishes would be lost
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah listed everything for בהמה, then גבן and חרום, which don't happen to animals, would not disqualify a כהן. So both lists are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote everything for an animal, I would say: whatever disqualifies an animal disqualifies a person. Then גבן and חרום, which do not exist in animals, would not disqualify a person either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer by testing the second option. Putting the full list only in the animal section fails too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blemishes happen only to people, like גבן (a blemish of the eyebrows) and חרום (a sunken nose). They would never appear in an animal list, so they would never transfer to כהנים. Each kind has blemishes unique to it, so the Torah has to write both lists.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with a blemish of the eyebrows (human-only)
A person with a sunken or flattened nose (human-only)
Which do not exist (in that kind)

steps.whatToRemember: The גזירה שוה of גרב and ילפת makes every shared blemish count for both people and animals. The Torah still writes two lists because each kind has blemishes the other cannot have: קלוט and חוטין only in animals, גבן and חרום only in people.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One wrote all of them regarding an animal,
I would say:
whatever disqualifies in an animal disqualifies in a person,
but a gibben and a charum, which do not exist in an animal,
would not disqualify in a person either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the answer begun in Step 12, covering the other option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that each list holds unique items that the other list cannot carry
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing everything in the animal list would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal-only list would leave out human-specific blemishes like גבן and חרום, so both lists are necessary.

steps.title: Why not write shared blemishes once and only link the lists with גרב and ילפת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a shorter way the Torah could have written the blemishes. Shared ones would appear once, unique ones in their own list, and גרב and ילפת in both lists as the link.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write all the shared blemishes in one place. The ones that are not found in the other case should be written by the animal, and the ones that are not found in the other case should be written by the person. גרב and ילפת should be written in both places, and the two lists can then be learned from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of steps 12 and 13. It says the Torah could still have saved words by writing each shared blemish only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12 and 13 showed that each list has blemishes the other list lacks, like קלוט for animals and גבן for people. But that only proves the unique blemishes must be written separately. The shared blemishes could have been written once, with גרב and ילפת in both lists serving as the bridge for the גזירה שוה, so why repeat all of them?

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, a name for God as the Author of the Torah
All of them in one place
That are not found in the other one
And let them be learned from each other

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write all of them in one place,
phrases.notes: Meaning all the blemishes that both lists share.

phrases.english: and those that are not found in the other —
let the Merciful One write them by the animal,
phrases.notes: Blemishes found only in animals, like קלוט.

phrases.english: and those that are not found in the other —
let Him write them by the person,
phrases.notes: Blemishes found only in people, like גבן.

phrases.english: and גרב and ילפת — here and here,
phrases.notes: Written in both lists to serve as the link for the גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: and let them be learned from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the challenge of step 11 so that it survives the answers of steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of steps 12 and 13, that both full lists are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unique blemishes explain why each list exists, but not why the shared blemishes are repeated. Writing shared items once and linking the lists with גרב and ילפת would be enough.

steps.title: The Torah repeats a passage to add something new
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with the rule of the school of רבי ישמעאל. When the Torah repeats a passage, it does so for the sake of the new detail added in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this follows what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: every passage that was said and then said again was repeated only for the new thing added in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a known style of the Torah. The Torah repeats the shared blemishes because each list adds new ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not always write in the shortest possible way. Sometimes it repeats a whole section just to teach one new point. Here the shared blemishes are repeated because each list also teaches blemishes found only in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the school (study hall) of רבי ישמעאל
Stated and then repeated
A new thing introduced in it

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah may repeat a whole passage just to add one new detail. So the shared blemishes appear in both lists because each list adds its own unique blemishes.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the repeated shared blemishes teach something new themselves. They are repeated only as the setting for the new blemishes.
steps.whyThisMatters: The school of רבי ישמעאל's rule is a general principle that appears across ש"ס to explain why the Torah repeats passages.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like the teaching of the school of Rabbi Yishmael,
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Every passage that was stated and repeated —
was repeated only
for the sake of the new thing introduced in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Repeating the shared blemishes seems wasteful, since they could have been written once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah's style is to repeat a full passage for the sake of a new detail, so the shared blemishes are repeated for the unique ones.

steps.title: Why does the Torah write the law of blemishes three times?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why the Torah needed to write that a מום disqualifies in three places: a כהן, קדשים, and a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Why do I need the Torah to write a blemish for a person, a blemish for sacrifices, and a blemish for a firstborn animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic. He asks why the law of מום appears three separate times in the Torah, and he will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion was about the lists of specific blemishes. רבא now asks about the basic rule itself, that a blemish disqualifies. If it is the same rule, it seems one source should be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? A question about a seemingly extra source
A physical blemish that disqualifies
Consecrated animals brought as קרבנות
A firstborn male kosher animal, holy from birth

phrases.english: Rava said:
Why do I need that the Merciful One wrote
a blemish for a person, a blemish for sacrifices,
phrases.notes: אדם here means a כהן doing the עבודה.

phrases.english: a blemish for a firstborn animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְמָה לִי דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about why the basic law of מום is written in three places.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why three separate verses are needed for the rule that a blemish disqualifies.

steps.title: Each case has its own stricter side, so each source is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that all three are needed. A כהן has more מצוות, and a בכור is itself offered on the מזבח, so one case cannot be learned from the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If the Torah wrote the blemish rule only for a person, I would say it applies only to him, because he is included in more מצוות. And a person cannot be learned from a firstborn animal, because the animal itself is offered on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the answer to his question. He shows that each case has something special about it, so no case can be learned from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule written only for a כהן could be explained by his special status: he is commanded in מצוות, so we would not apply it to animals. A rule written only for a בכור could be explained by the animal's special status: it is itself brought on the מזבח, which a כהן is not. Since each case is strict in its own way, the Torah must write each one.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary; each source teaches something needed
Included in more מצוות; a person is commanded, an animal is not
Cannot be learned from it
Is offered on the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'only for the person' do not appear in the text. The גמרא leaves them unsaid: 'since he was included in מצוות' means we would have limited the rule to him.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if the Merciful One had written a blemish for a person,
[I would say it applies only to him], since he was included in more מצוות.
A person cannot be learned from a firstborn animal,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכֵּן הוּא עַצְמוֹ קָרֵב לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: since it itself is offered on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא מוּם בְּאָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each case of מום is needed. A כהן is stricter because he is commanded in מצוות, and a בכור is stricter because it is itself offered on the מזבח, so neither can be learned from the other.

steps.title: Finishing the one-to-one comparisons
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his answer. קדשים cannot be learned from בכור, because a בכור is holy from birth. A כהן cannot be learned from קדשים, because קדשים are themselves offered. A בכור cannot be learned from קדשים, because קדשים have greater holiness.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sacrificial animals cannot be learned from a firstborn, since a firstborn's holiness starts from the womb. A person cannot be learned from sacrificial animals, since they themselves are offered on the altar. A firstborn cannot be learned from sacrificial animals, since their holiness is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא continues his answer from the last step. He shows each remaining pair, so that no single case can be learned from any one other case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pair fails because of a special feature. A בכור is holy from birth, which other קדשים are not. קדשים go onto the מזבח, which a כהן does not. קדשים have a 'bigger' holiness, which a בכור lacks. So for every pair, a special feature blocks the learning.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot be learned (literally, 'it does not come') from the other case
Its holiness is from the womb; a בכור becomes holy automatically at birth
They are offered on the מזבח
Its holiness is greater or wider (קדשים come in many types of offerings)

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals cannot be derived from a firstborn,
since its holiness is from the womb.
phrases.notes: A בכור is holy from birth, with no act of consecrating it.

phrases.english: A person cannot be derived from sacrificial animals,
phrases.notes: 'Person' here means a כהן.

phrases.english: since they themselves are offered.
A firstborn cannot be derived from sacrificial animals,
since their holiness is greater.
phrases.notes: Following Sefaria: there are many kinds of קדשים, but a בכור has only one kind of holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדָשִׁים מִבְּכוֹר לָא אָתֵי, שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתוֹ מֵרֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's answer from step 17 by covering the remaining one-to-one pairs.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Every pair has a special feature, so no single case can be learned from just one other case.

steps.title: Why not learn one case from the other two together?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Fine, one case cannot be learned from one other case. But maybe one case can be learned from the other two combined.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot come from one. But let one come from two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's conclusion. It suggests the Torah only needed to write two of the three cases, and the third could be learned from both together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא showed that each one-to-one comparison has a weak spot. But when two cases are combined, the weak spot of one may be covered by the other. If that works, one of the three verses is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: One from one; learning a case from a single other case
Let one be learned from two; learning a case from two cases combined

phrases.english: One cannot be derived from one,
let one be derived from two?

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 17-18 that all three verses are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that all three verses about מומין are needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if no one-to-one comparison works, a combination of two cases might teach the third. That would make one verse unnecessary.

steps.title: בכור cannot be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: from which two would you learn it? It tries leaving out בכור and learning it from כהן and קדשים. That fails, because those two have greater holiness and their rules apply even to non-firstborns.
steps.simpleTranslation: From which ones would you learn it? Should the Torah not write it by a firstborn, and you learn it from these? What about these? Their holiness is greater, and they apply to ordinary ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by testing each possible combination. Here it tests the first one: leaving out בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהן and קדשים share two features that בכור lacks. First, both have greater holiness: a כהן has many מצוות, and קדשים come in many types. Second, both apply to ordinary cases, meaning ordinary people and ordinary animals, not only to firstborns. Because the source cases are 'stronger' than בכור, we cannot learn בכור from them.

keyTerms.meaning: From which would it come? A challenge to name the actual combination
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳
What about these? What is special about the source cases that the target case lacks
Ordinary ones; people and animals that are not firstborns

steps.confusionAlert: פשוטין here does not mean 'simple' or 'obvious.' It means ordinary, non-firstborn people and animals. The point is that the source cases are not limited to firstborns.

phrases.english: From which should it be derived?!
Let the Merciful One not write it regarding a firstborn,
and let it be derived from these?
phrases.notes: These = כהן and קדשים.

phrases.english: What about these?
Their holiness is greater,
and they apply to ordinary (non-firstborn) ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵהֵי תֵּיתֵי?! לָא לִכְתֹּב רַחֲמָנָא בִּבְכוֹר, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by testing the first combination and showing it fails.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Testing each combination and showing a shared feature that blocks it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בכור could be learned from כהן and קדשים together.
steps.terutzMaskana: It cannot, because כהן and קדשים both have greater holiness and both apply to non-firstborns.

steps.title: קדשים cannot be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests leaving out קדשים and learning them from כהן and בכור. That fails too, because כהן and בכור are holy on their own. קדשים only become holy when someone consecrates them.
steps.simpleTranslation: By sacrificial animals, should you learn it from these? What about these? Their holiness comes on its own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second combination: leaving out קדשים. It rejects this option as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is holy simply by being born to a כהן, and a בכור is holy simply by being born first. קדשים need an owner to consecrate them. Since both source cases share an automatic holiness that קדשים lack, קדשים cannot be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Their holiness comes on its own, with no act of consecrating
An act of consecrating something; קדשים need this, but כהן and בכור do not

steps.whatToRemember: So far two combinations have failed. בכור cannot come from כהן plus קדשים, because those have greater holiness and apply to ordinary cases. קדשים cannot come from כהן plus בכור, because those are holy automatically. The third test, leaving out כהן, comes next.

phrases.english: Regarding sacrificial animals, let it be derived from these?
phrases.notes: These = כהן and בכור.

phrases.english: What about these? Their holiness comes on its own!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקָדָשִׁים, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ? מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן קְדוּשָּׁתָן מֵאֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer from step 20 by testing and rejecting the second combination.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning קדשים from כהן and בכור combined.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כהן and בכור share automatic holiness from birth, which קדשים lack.

steps.title: Testing whether a כהן's blemishes could be learned from the other two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries leaving out the blemishes of a person (a כהן) and learning them from בכור and קדשים. It rejects this because בכור and קדשים are themselves brought on the מזבח, while a כהן is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah not write the blemishes of a person, and we would learn them from these two cases? No. These two have something special: they themselves are offered on the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third and last test of the 'learn one from the other two' idea. Now the גמרא tries to learn the כהן's blemishes from בכור and קדשים, and it fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 failed for בכור and step 21 failed for קדשים. Here the missing case is the כהן. A בכור and קדשים are actually placed on the מזבח, so strict blemish rules make more sense for them. A כהן only serves at the מזבח and is not offered on it, so his rules cannot be learned from theirs.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it come (be learned)
From those (the other two cases)
Are offered (as a sacrifice)
Onto the altar

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'בְּאָדָם' at the start finish a sentence that began earlier: 'Let the Torah not write blemishes for a person.' Here 'a person' means the כהן.

phrases.english: (Let the Torah not write blemishes) in a person, and learn them from these?
phrases.notes: Continues the sentence from the previous line. 'These' means בכור and קדשים.

phrases.english: What about these, which have the feature that
phrases.notes: Standard 'מה ל...' rejection formula: the source cases have a special feature.

phrases.english: they themselves are offered on the altar!
phrases.notes: A כהן is not offered, so his case is weaker.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן הֵן עַצְמָן קְרֵיבִין לְגַבֵּי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third parallel test, after steps 20 (בכור) and 21 (קדשים). This one leaves out the כהן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the כהן's blemishes from the combination of בכור and קדשים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both source cases share a stricter feature the כהן lacks: they are themselves offered on the מזבח.

steps.title: Conclusion: all three cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: Since no case can be learned from one other case or from the other two together, the Torah must state the blemish laws for כהן, בכור and קדשים separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are all needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole discussion. Every attempt to skip one of the three cases failed, so all three must be written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For every possible pair of sources, the two share a stricter feature that the third case lacks. כהן and קדשים both have greater holiness and apply to ordinary, non-firstborn cases, which בכור lacks. כהן and בכור are both holy automatically, which קדשים lack. בכור and קדשים are both offered on the מזבח, which a כהן is not. So no case can be learned from the other two, and each verse is necessary.

keyTerms.meaning: They are (all) needed
Priest
Firstborn animal
Consecrated animals (sacrifices)

steps.whatToRemember: The Torah states the rule that a מום disqualifies three separate times: for a כהן, for קדשים and for a בכור. None of these verses is extra. Each single case has a special feature, and each pair shares a feature the third case lacks, so no case can be learned from one other case or from two.

phrases.english: They are needed.
phrases.notes: The standard one-word close of a צריכותא discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the failure of all three 'learn from two' attempts (steps 20 to 22).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three blemish lists (כהן, בכור, קדשים) are necessary. None can be derived from the others.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the extra blemishes for a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that a person has blemishes beyond the animal list, and asks where this comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'In addition to these, there are more for a person.' From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its Torah source. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that a כהן can be disqualified by more blemishes than an animal. Some of these do not even look like real defects. The גמרא wants to know which verse says a person has a wider list.

keyTerms.meaning: In addition to them (beyond the animal list)
A person (here, a כהן)
From where are these words (learned)? A request for a source.
Blemishes

phrases.english: "In addition to these, (there are more blemishes) in a person."
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: From where are these matters (learned)?
phrases.notes: The standard request for a Torah source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the צריכותא discussion and starts a new topic based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that teaches a כהן has extra blemishes beyond those of animals.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a כהן must look like the rest of זרע אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן brings the verse 'any man who has a blemish, of the seed of אהרן'. He reads it to mean a כהן must be like (equal to) the other descendants of אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: because the verse says, "Any man who has a blemish, from the seed of אהרן". This means a man who is equal to (looks like) the rest of the seed of אהרן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question from step 24 by bringing a verse. It explains why a person has extra blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads 'מזרע אהרן' as a standard: a כהן must be similar in appearance to the other כהנים. So anything that makes him look noticeably different disqualifies him, even if it would not be a blemish in an animal. That is why a person's list is longer.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא of ארץ ישראל who gives the source
A verse
The descendants of אהרן (the כהנים)
Equal to (looks like the rest of) his family

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains the many human-only blemishes in the rest of the פרק. A כהן is disqualified by anything that makes him stand out in appearance from other כהנים, not only by physical defects.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these extra signs are 'real blemishes' in the animal sense. They disqualify because the כהן looks different from other כהנים, not because his body is damaged.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: because the verse says:
phrases.notes: The attribution is merged into this answer step.

phrases.english: "Any man who has a blemish
phrases.notes: ויקרא כא:כא

phrases.english: of the seed of Aaron",
phrases.notes: The key words for the derivation.

phrases.english: (meaning) a man who is equal to the seed of Aaron.
phrases.notes: He must look like the other כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the source question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse 'מזרע אהרן' requires a כהן to be similar to the other descendants of אהרן. So appearance-based differences count as extra blemishes for a person.
